S76.01.note: "Text only" appears only for a model with no other capability chip. The routing rule itself is not visible on screen.
steps: Sign in and look at the composer at the bottom of a chat.
Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Click All models.
Open the info button of a model row (its name is "About" followed by the model name).
Read the Capabilities section. A model with no other capability shows "Text only". Compare with Expected: text input is recorded per model, and chat models accept text.
S76.01.where: Model name button in the composer footer > All models > info button on a model row > Capabilities

S76.02.note: No screen shows a text-output value. The only related word is "Text only" (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ModelCatalogue.tsx), which describes capability chips, not output.
steps: Send a plain text message to any model.
Check that a text answer appears in the chat, as Expected says models produce text for chat tasks.
S76.02.where: Inside every chat reply (no separate control for text output)

S76.03.needs: a photo file (PNG or JPEG) and a chat with a model that cannot read images
S76.03.note: The round + button has no text label in the code. I did not confirm that the chat shows the server refusal text word for word.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer, then click All models.
Click the Vision chip under Filter by capability. Each listed model should show Vision under Capabilities.
Pick a model that does not show Vision, click the round + button at the left of the composer, and click Add photos & files.
Choose a photo, type a question about it, and send.
Compare with Expected: the app should refuse the image turn or reroute it. The server refusal text is "The selected model cannot read images. Choose a vision-capable model."
S76.03.where: Model name button in the composer footer > All models > Vision chip under Filter by capability

labels.text: Remove some images or split the request.

S76.04.needs: several image files and a model with an image limit (the limit is not shown on screen)
S76.04.note: The per-model image count is held in the registry and is not shown in the picker. I did not confirm how the chat displays the error.
steps: Pick a model in the composer footer.
Click the round + button at the left of the composer.
Click Add photos & files and choose more images than the model accepts.
Send the message and read the error. Expected: the request is checked against the model's image limit.
The server error reads "The selected model takes up to N images in one request. Remove some images or split the request."
S76.04.where: Round + button at the left of the composer > Add photos & files, then send

S76.06.needs: a PDF file and a chat model
S76.06.note: The picker has no PDF label, so which models read PDFs natively is not visible on screen. The page limit is checked on the server.
steps: Click the round + button at the left of the composer.
Click Add photos & files and choose a PDF.
Ask a question that only the PDF's text can answer, then send.
Check that the answer uses the PDF content, which Expected says goes to models that accept PDFs natively.
S76.06.where: Round + button at the left of the composer > Add photos & files, then send a question about the PDF

S76.07.note: I did not trace how the composer handles an audio file attachment. The check here covers only the picker filter and the capability card.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer, then click All models.
Click the Audio in chip under Filter by capability.
Open the info button of a listed model and read Capabilities. It should show Audio in.
Compare with Expected: the list shows only models that accept audio input.
S76.07.where: Model name button in the composer footer > All models > Audio in chip

labels.text: Voice input is not supported in this browser. Try Chrome or Edge.

S76.08.needs: a microphone and a browser that allows microphone access (the app suggests Chrome or Edge)
S76.08.note: The transcription model's name is not shown on screen. The button is wired in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx.
steps: Click the microphone button labelled Start voice input in the composer.
Allow microphone access when the browser asks.
Say a short sentence, then click the button again to stop.
Check that the spoken words appear in the message box, as Expected says dictation uses the registry transcription model.
S76.08.where: Composer microphone button labelled Start voice input

S76.09.note: The realtime audio model's name is not shown on the voice screen.
steps: Click the button labelled Start voice mode in the composer.
Allow microphone access when the browser asks.
Say a short sentence out loud.
Check that captions or a transcript of your words appear on the voice screen, as Expected says live voice starts on the registry model.
S76.09.where: Composer button labelled Start voice mode

S76.10.note: The button only appears on assistant replies that have text. Its wiring is in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx.
steps: Send a message and wait until the full reply is finished.
Hover over the reply and find the button labelled Read message aloud.
Click it and listen for speech from the speakers or headphones.
Click the button again, now labelled Stop reading message, to stop.
Check that the speech comes from a model the registry chose, as Expected says. The model is not named on screen.
S76.10.where: Read message aloud button under an assistant reply

S76.11.needs: a microphone and speakers or headphones
S76.11.note: This is the same screen as S76.09. No separate control chooses the speech-to-speech model.
steps: Click Start voice mode in the composer.
Allow microphone access.
Ask a spoken question.
Listen for the spoken reply and compare with Expected: live voice uses a speech-to-speech model for spoken replies.
S76.11.where: Composer button labelled Start voice mode, then ask a question out loud

S76.14.needs: none (plan limits, if any, were not checked)
S76.14.note: If the composer refuses, it shows "Image generation is not available from this chat." (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx).
steps: Click the round + button at the left of the composer.
Click Create image.
Type a picture prompt and send.
Check that an image appears in the reply.
Open All models and click the Image out chip to see which models make images, then compare with Expected.
S76.14.where: Round + button at the left of the composer > Create image

S76.15.needs: a picture file; a model list that includes an edit-capable model
S76.15.note: The menu flow is read from the code. I did not confirm that every step appears in the order given.
steps: Click the round + button, then Add photos & files, and attach one picture.
Click Create image.
Open the Image model menu and choose a model.
Open the Attached image action menu and pick Edit (Mask edit appears only with a second mask image).
Type the change, send, and compare with Expected: a model that cannot edit should show the notice "... cannot edit an attached image."
S76.15.where: Round + button > Add photos & files (attach a picture) > Create image > Image model menu > Attached image action menu

S76.17.needs: none (plan limits, if any, were not checked)
steps: Click the round + button, then click Create video.
Type a short prompt.
Open the Video length, Video quality and Video aspect ratio menus and pick values.
Send and wait for the job to finish.
Compare the length and aspect ratio of the result with what you picked. Expected: video requests are checked against the model's durations and sizes.
S76.17.where: Round + button at the left of the composer > Create video

S76.19.needs: a generated video and speakers or headphones
S76.19.note: I found no audio switch in apps/web/features. The server decides generateAudio from the model or the request (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts, line 1208).
steps: Generate a video (see S76.17).
Play the finished video with the speakers on.
Check whether the video has sound, and compare with Expected: it has audio only where the model supports it.
S76.19.where: Sound in a finished generated video

labels.text: The selected model cannot load skills. Choose a tool-capable model.

steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer, then click All models.
Click the Tools chip under Filter by capability.
Open the info button of a listed model and read Capabilities. It should show Tools.

Compare with Expected: tool-dependent turns go only to tool-capable models. A model without tools shows the refusal "The selected model cannot load skills. Choose a tool-capable model." when a skill is used.
S76.21.where: Model name button in the composer footer > All models > Tools chip under Filter by capability

S76.22.note: No control or label shows parallel tool support. It is set in the registry (packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/harnesses.json) and used in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts.
steps: Send a request that needs two independent tools (for example a search and a file lookup, if connected).
Look at the tool cards in the reply and check whether the calls ran together, as Expected says the tool loop uses parallel support.
S76.22.where: Inside a reply that calls several tools at once

S76.23.note: No screen says agentic or multi-round. The closest visible word is the Tools chip (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ModelCatalogue.tsx), which only shows tool calling.
steps: Send a request that needs a second tool call after the first one's result.
Check that the reply shows a second tool step after the first.
S76.23.where: Inside a reply that uses tools one after another

S76.26.needs: a paid account to see levels marked "not included"
S76.26.note: Some models have no effort slider. The footer hides it when there is no explicit effort ladder.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Open the Reasoning effort panel and look at the levels offered.
Levels are named Direct, Brief, Quick, Balanced, Deep, Extended and Maximum. Only the levels the model supports should appear.
Pick a level, send a message, and compare with Expected: each surface offers and sends only the levels the registry records.
S76.26.where: Model name button in the composer footer > Reasoning effort panel

S76.28.note: Trimming or refusing over-long chats happens on the server and shows no visible notice in the code I read. Only a server log line was found.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer, then click All models.
Open the info button of a model row.
Read the Context ceiling value (for example in K or M).
Compare with Expected: the value shows the model's context window.
S76.28.where: Model name button in the composer footer > All models > info button on a model row > Context ceiling

S76.29.note: The cap on requests is applied on the server. I found no visible message for it.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer, then click All models.
Open the info button of a model row.
Read the Output ceiling value.
Compare with Expected: the value shows the model's output-token limit.
S76.29.where: Model name button in the composer footer > All models > info button on a model row > Output ceiling

S76.31.note: No streaming control or label appears on screen. The transport is chosen in the provider code.
steps: Send a prompt that asks for a long answer.
Watch whether text appears before the answer is finished, as Expected says streaming depends on the model.
S76.31.where: Reply text while it is being written

labels.text: Switching models here starts a new prompt cache

S76.32.needs: an existing chat with earlier replies
S76.32.note: The hint appears only when earlier turns hold a cache, so it may not show in a brand-new chat.
steps: Open a chat that already has at least one earlier reply.
Click the model name button in the composer footer and choose a different model.
Read the note under the picker: "Switching models here starts a new prompt cache".
Compare with Expected: the app shows the cache effect of switching models.
S76.32.where: Model name button in the composer footer, in a chat that already has replies > choose a different model

S76.34.note: I searched ModelCatalogue, ComposerFooter, ChatComposerNew and packages/ui/unified-chat for region or residency wording and found nothing per model. Public pages such as apps/web/app/data-use/page.tsx are general, not per model.
S76.34.where: No screen shows a model's region in the picker; a refused route has no visible text found

S76.35.note: I searched the picker and settings for retention wording and found no per-model retention label. Routing uses retention in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx and packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts; effects are not visible on screen.
S76.35.where: No per-model retention text in the picker

S76.37.needs: none (a model in its last 30 days before retirement may not exist)
S76.37.note: Models past their retirement date are dropped from the picker. The code comment at apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx (around line 312) says so.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer, then click All models.
Look at each row's tags for Preview, Experimental, Beta or Alpha, and for Coming soon.
Look for grey text "Leaving <date>" under a row name. It appears only within 30 days before retirement.
Try to pick a "Coming soon" model and check it does not start, as Expected says pickers exclude or label such models.
S76.37.where: Model name button in the composer footer > All models, then look at row tags and the "Leaving" note

S76.38.needs: a platform admin account (not a normal Free or paid account)
S76.38.note: The registry data is shown only in the admin Routes panel; the per-route price is described in the panel intro text but I did not confirm a price column. The routing ranking part of Expected (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1099 zero-retention filter and :1169 cache-affinity ranking) has no visible control and is inner behaviour, so a tester cannot see it from the UI. Composer catalogue at ComposerFooter.tsx:1571 is a model picker, not a route display, and was not used.
steps: Sign in with a platform admin account and go to /operator.
Click the Routes tab.
Read the heading Routes and the line below it, which says every route the registry declares is listed with what it costs.
Click a route row to expand it.
Look for the detail labels Cache class and Data retention on the expanded row, and compare with Expected (cache class and data retention per provider route).
S76.38.where: Open the /operator page (platform admin account only), then click the tab labelled Routes (the tab text is lowercase "routes" and is shown capitalised). The heading on the panel reads Routes.
